reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played both Kaboom! copies into the Fuzzy Wurm Crawler and then Duck and Cover. That is literally my whole playable hand: two of my five cards are switched off because they want Sparks and I have none, and nothing else in the hand makes a Spark, so the only three cards I can touch cost exactly the three energy I have. Two Kaboom! take the Crawler from 46 to 32 and stick Pyro on it, and the 5 Block from Duck and Cover swallows the incoming 4 without a scratch. I did not have to weigh anything; I just spent everything because there was nothing to hold it for and no cost to spending it.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Honestly, no. The only thing that looked like a choice for a moment was whether Duck and Cover was worth an energy against a 4-damage hit, but since there is no third attack to spend that energy on and no reason to keep a card in hand, playing it is free value rather than a tradeoff. I also looked twice at Ka-pow! and Firework Finale hoping the Kaboom! attacks would bank a Spark on hit and open them up mid-turn, but nothing printed on them says so and the page says the Spark power is absent, so that was a dead end rather than a considered line. The hand plays itself.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: Very little, which is my main complaint. In pure resource terms I gave up nothing: no card kept, no energy floated, no future turn compromised, and the only damage on the table was fully absorbed. What the line gave up is any chance of ever using the two Spark cards this turn, and by exhausting my playable cards I go into the next turn with a hand that is entirely redraw plus two blocked cards that will still be blocked unless a Spark source appears. So the cost is not paid this turn; it is that 40% of my hand is inert paper and I had no way to change that.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. Against a bigger attack I still play the same three cards in the same order, because there is nothing stronger to convert the energy into and 5 Block is all the defense I own. Against a non-attack intent, a buff, or a block, Duck and Cover becomes wasted Block, but it still costs me nothing real to play, so I would play it anyway rather than end the turn with an unspent energy and a card I have no plan for. The intent line is decoration here; the hand determines the turn entirely.

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
